newsitem.title: USA: Atlas sees positive cash flow from purchases.
newsitem.headline: Atlas sees positive cash flow from purchases.

text.p: Atlas Corp on Tuesday said recent acquisitions in Bolivia returned the company to an operating status and would generate positive cash flow.

Gregg Shafter, Atlas vice president for project development, said the company would now focus efforts in Bolivia "on expansion of operations, including contemplated gold exploration concentrating on areas in and around our existing infrastructure there."
Atlas said in the fourth quarter its Andacaba Mine in the Potosi district of southern Bolivia produced 998 metric tonnes of zinc, 386 tonnes of lead and 135,662 ounces of silver.

The mine is operated by Arisur Inc, acquired by Atlas in October 1996. The subsidiary also operates the Don Francisco Mine, which underwent development work during the last quarter of 1996, resulting in minimal ore production.

Arisur has begun an expansion program to increase mill capacity to 450 tonnes per day from 200 tonnes per day, which restricted Andacaba production during the latter part of the quarter. Expansion programs for both mines are expected to be completed in the first half of 1997, Atlas said.
In addition to the Andacaba and Don Francisco mines, the company recently acquired the Koyamayu zinc, lead and silver property, also in southern Bolivia.

Based on recent limited production, the company said, it expects to start commercial production at Koyamayu at a rate of 50 to 100 tonnes per day during the second half of 1997. Based on prior production, grades for the Koyamayu ore are estimated to be 18 percent zinc, 4.0 percent lead and 3.5 ounces of silver per tonne.

Atlas said it also purchased the Vicormo Mill, located within 90 kilometers of Arisur's current operations. A capital investment of about $250,000 will be required to put the facility into operation later this year at a rate of 250 tonnes per day.

The company said it planned to use the mill to process ore from surrounding mines in the second half of 1997. It is currently evaluating its potential to process ore from the Don Francisco and Koyamayu properties.

Atlas also said it expected the southeastern Oregon facility of majority-owned Cornerstone Industrial Minerals Corp will begin production of the industrial mineral perlite later this month. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
